chapters.title: What people clock in ten seconds
chapters.teaser: The first impression you give, whether you meant to or not.

chapters.title: Your red flag (yes, you have one)
chapters.teaser: The habit everyone's noticed and nobody's mentioned.

chapters.title: How you sabotage love
chapters.teaser: Your signature move for making romance harder than it needs to be.

chapters.title: Friends and work: the receipts
chapters.teaser: What your coworkers and group chat would say if they were honest.

chapters.title: Okay fine, the fix (Bom made me)

text.first-impression: Mu, new people tend to feel calmer. You're solid, unbothered, the human equivalent of a very good sofa. Ten seconds in they think: this person could handle a crisis. You could, and you have, several times, without making a fuss. You don't perform, don't oversell, don't rush. What they also clock: you're hard to read. Is Mu happy? Annoyed? Asleep with eyes open? Nobody knows. Not even, on some days, you. You've perfected the neutral face so well that you sometimes forget there's weather behind it. Let someone in on the forecast sometimes.
text.your-red-flag: Here's the flag: you don't move. Physically, emotionally, philosophically. You've had the same opinion since 2014 and you're proud of it. New idea? You'll consider it. For about two years. And when you're upset, you go silent and heavy, like weather that refuses to break, while everyone tiptoes around the mountain wondering what they did. Stability is a real gift. Stubbornness dressed up as stability is just stubbornness with better posture. Learn which one you're doing, and admit it when it's the second. Hint: if you can't explain why, it's probably the second one.
text.how-you-sabotage-love: In love you're loyal, protective, and as reliable as sunrise. Partners feel safe. They also feel occasionally bored, and sometimes lonely next to you, because you show love by doing and very rarely by saying. You fix the shelf. You don't say I love how you laugh. Your sabotage is assuming they know. They don't. You also stay too long in things because leaving feels like relocating a mountain. Say one loving thing out loud once a week. It won't kill you. I checked the research. It's fine. Start with something easy, like I like having you here.
text.friends-and-work: On the job you're the rock. Deadlines, crises, the person people trust with the things that actually matter. But you resist change, new systems, new tools, new ideas, until it's very late and slightly embarrassing. With friends you're the one who shows up, helps carry the sofa, never forgets the important date. But you rarely ask for help yourself, so people genuinely don't know when you need it. They're not psychic, Mu. Give them a chance to carry something for you, even something small. They'd actually love to. People like repaying mountains.
text.the-lie: Your favorite lie: I'm not really an emotional person. Mu, you have feelings the size of a mountain range. You just keep them underground, where they come out as tiredness, irritation, or a sudden eruption over how someone loaded the dishwasher. You also tell yourself change is risky. Sometimes it is. But staying exactly the same is also a risk. It's just a slower one, so you don't notice it until you're standing in the same spot, wondering why the view never changes. Move one rock this month. Just one. See how the view changes.
text.the-fix: Now the fix, by order of Bom. Try one new thing a month: a food, a route, an opinion, a playlist. Say one feeling out loud a day, even a tiny one. I'm tired counts. Ask a friend for help with something small so everyone learns you're allowed to need things. In love, use words as well as actions, at least once a week. You're the steadiest person in most rooms. Imagine how good you'd be with a little movement. A mountain with a breeze. Honestly, iconic. Don't tell Bom I said that.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Mu, that opinion is old enough to have its own birthday.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: It's called refusing to try the new café. For three years.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Also, fixing their shelf isn't saying 'I love you'. Use words.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu is the most reliable person ever.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Yes. Reliable people can still say 'I'm sad'. Try it.

spring.intro: Spring Mu, you were born while Wood was in charge and Wood controls Earth. So you grew up being pushed on and learned to just stand there. You're the mountain who takes it. People see someone calm, steady and impossible to rattle. Your friends know you've been annoyed about the same thing for over a year and said nothing. Your red flag is silent endurance. You let people put roots through you and then act shocked when you crack. In love you go along with their plans until you suddenly don't. At work you absorb extra tasks without a word. The fix: complain early, while it's small and nobody needs a geologist.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You've been quietly furious since last spring. Ever thought about mentioning it, Mu?

summer.intro: Summer Mu, your season belonged to Fire and Fire feeds Earth, so you're a sun-warmed mountain: solid, confident and completely unwilling to move. People clock you as dependable. Then they try to change the plan. Your red flag is stubbornness wearing a calm face. You don't argue. You simply don't budge, and somehow that's worse. In love partners feel like they're negotiating with geography. At work you're reliable and also the reason the new system took nine months to roll out. The fix: when someone suggests a change, say let's try it before you say but. You'll still be a mountain afterward. Promise.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Mu is so dependable! Trying one new thing won't change that, promise.

autumn.intro: Autumn Mu, Metal was in command when you arrived and Earth gives birth to Metal, so you express yourself through doing. You're the friend who helps you move flat and then says nothing about your feelings, ever. People see someone useful and kind. Your friends know you'd rather assemble furniture than have one emotional conversation. Your red flag is acts of service as a hiding place. In love you show care with deeds and dodge every talk about what it means. At work you're the workhorse nobody thinks to promote because you never ask. The fix: say one feeling out loud this week. Not a fact. A feeling. I'll wait.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You built their entire wardrobe and said zero feelings. Typical Mu love letter.

winter.intro: Winter Mu, your season belonged to Water and Earth controls Water, so you're a dam with a calm face. You manage everyone's emotions, including your own, mostly by not having them in public. People see the steady one. Your friends call you in a crisis because you won't panic. Your red flag is control dressed up as calm. You decide what counts as an overreaction, including other people's. In love partners feel handled rather than met. At work you keep the peace so firmly that problems never get named. The fix: let somebody else's feelings be messy without managing them. Just listen. Don't fix. Don't shrink it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Mu is the calm in every storm. It's okay to have a storm sometimes.

earth.intro: Earth days are Earth's own season, Mu, and you got a double helping. Mountain on mountain. People see someone solid and reliable. Your friends see someone who decided in 2019 and hasn't revisited. Your red flag is immovability passing as calm. In love partners feel like they're negotiating with geography. At work your no is final before anyone finishes the pitch. The fix: change one small opinion this month, on purpose, and notice that the mountain is still standing.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Mu, 'I've always done it this way' is a fact, not an argument.

strength.strong: Strong chart, Mu, and you know it. Solid ground, plenty of support, absolutely no intention of changing your mind. The blind spot: you're immovable and you think that's a virtue. Sometimes it is. Often it's just rigid. You order the same meal, take the same route, have the same argument with the same outcome. Partners can feel like they're talking to a beautiful wall. At work you resist every new idea on principle. The fix: change one routine a week. A new café. A different route home. Let life surprise you once.
strength.weak: Weak chart, Mu, so you've had to become the steady one without much backing, and you overdo it. The blind spot: you carry everything and tell nobody. Everyone leans on you because you never wobble in public. In private, you wobble plenty. In love you take your partner's stress as your job. At work you take on more rather than admit you're full. The fix: say I can't take that on, once this month. Watch the world carry on perfectly fine. Then do it again.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood. You're all growth, plans and ambition, and you never stop reaching. Cute. Also exhausting. You start projects faster than you finish them, and you think rest is for people with fewer goals. You argue to win rather than to understand. Yeon's prescription: prune. Finish one thing before starting another. Say you're right once a week and mean it. A tree that never stops growing eventually just falls over.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood. Starting things is hard for you, so you just... don't. You wait for the right moment, and the right moment is apparently very busy. You have plans in drafts and ideas in your notes app from three years ago. Yeon's prescription: take the first ugly step today. Send the email. Sign up for the class. Buy the plant. Momentum isn't a mood. It's a decision you make before you feel ready.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire. Everything feels urgent, out loud or only on the inside, and your feelings arrive with sirens on even when nobody else can hear them. You're bright company, and you're also impulsive, and you've sent messages you'd love to unsend. Yeon's prescription: wait one night before any big decision. Drink water, literally and spiritually. Let your calmest friend talk you down before your wildest one hypes you up. Your spark is great. Your house fires are not.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire. You're lovely, but you're keeping your light on its dimmest setting. You hang back, never celebrate yourself, and assume people won't notice you anyway. That isn't modesty. It's hiding with good manners. Yeon's prescription: be seen. Post the thing, wear the color, tell the joke out loud. Go outside in the sun. People can't love what they can't see, and you're worth seeing.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth. You're stable. Very stable. Possibly too stable. Same restaurant, same route, same opinion, same worry on repeat. You call it reliable. It's also a rut with nice furniture. Yeon's prescription: one new thing a week. It doesn't have to be big. A new food, a new walk, a new person to talk to. Growth needs a little mess, and you can tidy it up afterwards if it makes you feel better.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth. You're a little all over the place. Plans change, meals get skipped, home is wherever you last dropped your bag. You're adaptable, sure, but you never quite feel settled. Yeon's prescription: routine. Boring, beautiful routine. Same bedtime, real meals, one corner of your home that's only yours. Grounded people make better decisions. Yes, I'm looking directly at you.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal. You're sharp, critical, and your opinions come with edges. You decide fast and judge faster. People respect you, and also slightly fear your face in meetings. Yeon's prescription: soften up. Ask before you judge. Let some things stay imperfect. Cry at a film. You can keep your standards and still let people near you without running a full security check first.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal. Boundaries? Never heard of them. You say yes when you mean no, answer messages at midnight, and lend people your time without ever getting it back. Yeon's prescription: one no a week, with no explanation attached. Declutter something. Unsubscribe, unfollow, unclench. A boundary isn't mean. It's just a door with a lock, and you're allowed to own the key.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water. You think. And think. And then think about what you thought. You feel everything and analyze it until it turns to soup. Your intuition is brilliant. Your sleep schedule is not. Yeon's prescription: get out of your head and into your body. Walk, cook, lift something heavy. Put a timer on the overthinking. Then go and live a little.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water. You go, go, go and never stop to feel anything. Rest is for the weak, reflection is a waste of time, and you've been busy for about five years straight. Yeon's prescription: sit still. Ten minutes. No phone. Write one honest line before bed. Your feelings don't disappear because you're running. They just wait for you, patiently, like a bill.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood. You started a new life plan on Monday. It's Wednesday. New plan.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: All that drive is wonderful. Finishing one thing will feel even better.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: three dramatic exits from group chats this year. I counted.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion lights rooms up. Count to ten before the big reply.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth: same order, same route, same hoodie since 2019. I see you.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness makes people feel safe. Try one new thing for fun.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal. Your honesty has made two baristas reconsider their careers.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your clarity is a gift. Wrap it in a little kindness.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you've overthought this reading three times already. Stop.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is beautiful. Come back to shore when it gets heavy.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: No Wood, no ambition. Your five-year plan is 'see what happens'.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood just means growth needs a nudge. One small goal is plenty.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: No Fire. You'd describe your best night out ever as 'fine'. Show some spark!

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can mute your joy. Do one thing just because it's fun.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth. You've changed flat, job and hair color twice this year.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth makes it hard to settle. A simple routine is grounding.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal. You've never said no to anyone in your life, have you?

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal means boundaries take practice. Start with one tiny no.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: No Water. Someone cried in front of you and you offered a snack.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can hide feelings. Name one out loud today.
